podcast.title: Founding (1989)
podcast.body: Merge Records, an indie label based in Durham, North Carolina, was established in 1989 by two members of the band Superchunk. They founded it because they faced difficulties in finding a major label or subsidiary to release their own music. "Their label was an Indie from Durham, North Carolina called Merge. The company was established in 1989 by two people from a band called SuperChunk, and theirs was the same story that we've heard again and again. They couldn't find any major or major label subsidiary to release their music, so they just created their own company and did it themselves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: North Carolina Indie Label (1989-Present)
podcast.body: A North Carolina label that had been struggling since its founding in 1989. Its fortunes significantly improved after nurturing Arcade Fire, whose massive online following and subsequent offline success boosted Merge's profile. "Merge had been struggling along since 1989, before they encountered Arcade Fire, which thanks to music blogs and file sharing, built a massive online following that eventually moved into the offline world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Discovery of Arcade Fire (2003)
podcast.body: Merge Records first took notice of Arcade Fire after their 2003 debut EP, *Us Kids No*, and subsequently requested a full album from the band, initiating their long-standing partnership. "that release attracted the attention of merge records, which was an indie label based out of Durham, North Carolina. They liked what the band was doing, and they asked for a full album."

podcast.title: Indie Label Success (Post-2004)
podcast.body: Founded in 1989 by members of SuperChunk in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, Merge Records struggled for years. Its work began to pay off significantly in late 2004 when the Montreal-based Arcade Fire, a Merge act, gained popularity, becoming one of the best-selling independent artists of 2005. "They struggled for years, and it wasn't until late 2004 that this work really began to pay off. That's when a Merge Act, the Montreal-based Arcade Fire, began to take off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Best-Selling Album: Funeral
podcast.body: Arcade Fire's *Funeral* became Merge Records' best-selling album at the time, indicating its immense commercial success for an independent release and for the label. "Funeral had been the best selling album ever."

podcast.title: Continued Success: Neon Bible
podcast.body: Arcade Fire's *Neon Bible* album surpassed the sales of *Funeral*, becoming an even greater commercial success for Merge Records and further solidifying their relationship. "And Neon Bible did even better."

podcast.title: Early Struggles and Arcade Fire Breakthrough
podcast.body: The label faced "rocky" times for approximately a dozen years until Arcade Fire's *Funeral* album came along, which led to a significant explosion in the label's fortunes and global recognition. "It was rocky for about a dozen years, but then Arcade Fire comes along with Funeral, and things just blew up."

podcast.title: Independent Label for Arcade Fire
podcast.body: Merge Records is an independent record label based in Durham, North Carolina, and is the label to which Arcade Fire is signed. Despite its indie status, it has been the home for critically acclaimed and globally recognized albums such as "The Suburbs." "Arcade Fire is an independent band from Montreal that records for an indie label in Durham, North Carolina."
